evidence.caveat: HELD-03 is held by the text LLM condition too, so part of this pattern is prompt-level ambiguity, not graph-specific; the graph condition produced 4 such holds vs 1 for text.

candidate_causes_ranked.summary: The graph renderer exposes every operation with an explicit authorization field (null when absent) and only emits AUTHORIZED_BY edges when structured authorization exists. In this cache the model reads a null authorization / absent AUTHORIZED_BY edge on an evidence-backed REVISE or SUPERSEDE as 'prior record changed without authorization'. The deterministic text baseline and the text LLM condition instead accept those changes as explicitly evidenced.

HAS_OPERATION/PROPOSES edges attach the operation node to the new/changed candidate record only. For HELD-01 the model treated the operation-selected record r2 as the resulting state and reported the untouched candidate record r1's claim as omitted, causing coverage + preservation FAILs, while the text condition accepted the same transition citing both candidate records.

The shared verifier prompt says an explicit operation alone does not authorize a change and requires reason codes for unauthorized prior changes, without stating that evidence-backed REVISE/SUPERSEDE is an explicit authorized change (structured authorization is required only for DELETE). HELD-03 is held for this reason in both graph and text conditions, so this candidate is representation-independent.

evidence.interpretation: Not supported as the explanation for these four cases: the false-hold cases are shorter than the mean graph input (see means), and the correlations are descriptive only and would be unstable at n=13.

candidate_causes_ranked.summary: Graph serialization is larger on average, but the false-hold cases are not the long-input cases: their graph inputs are shorter than the correct-accept mean, and their char ratios are near the median. This hypothesis is not supported by the cached data.

No cached verdict is UNCERTAIN and there are no verifier errors. 7/52 calls needed one JSON-repair retry, but only one of those retries (HELD-02 graph) is among the false holds; HELD-01/03/07 were first-attempt valid JSON. Retries do inflate reported output tokens.
